title: Triangulation

D0.outcome: Explains triangulation as losing a tempo with the king by a detour of an odd number of moves, to change who is to move.

D1.outcome: In a given position, finds the three-square detour that changes the move.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled king-and-pawn positions, recognises when the detour wins and when the defender can answer in kind.

D3.outcome: Predicts the result by counting tempi and verifies with the tablebase.

misconceptions: Opposition is a fixed pattern of squares (and the king cannot lose a tempo).
sources: sources/sheets/emlasker_common-sense.md §4.19 (a tempo-losing king manoeuvre costing an odd number of moves)
sources/sheets/nimzowitsch_my-system.md §4 idea 18 (tripartite manoeuvre as an extra lens; do not retire the opposition)
conditions: The triangle squares are free and safe and the defender cannot lose a tempo himself.
contrasts: The defender has a spare move or can triangulate too.
Dropping the opposition for the tripartite manoeuvre; the opposition remains core.
A position where the move cannot matter.
